SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE

Riverside Hospital outpatient endoscopy unit (fictional)
Upper endoscopy report

Patient: Casey Moreau (fictional)
Synthetic record: SYN-GI-2004
Procedure date: October 19, 2026
Setting: Hospital outpatient department
Endoscopist: Dr. Ana Lucia Prieto, MD (fictional)

Procedure
EGD with through-the-scope balloon dilation of a distal esophageal stricture.

Indication
Progressive solid-food dysphagia; prior barium study showed a distal esophageal narrowing.

Description of procedure
The upper endoscope was passed into the esophagus. A smooth, benign-appearing stricture was found in the distal esophagus, 2 cm above the gastroesophageal junction, measuring about 12 mm. The endoscope traversed the stricture and was advanced to the second portion of the duodenum. A TTS balloon dilation was performed across the stricture, sequentially to 13.5, 15 and 16.5 mm, with a mild mucosal tear and no bleeding. No biopsies were taken because the stricture appeared benign and peptic.

Impression
Benign-appearing distal esophageal stricture, dilated with a balloon to 16.5 mm.

Recommendations
Continue twice-daily proton pump inhibitor. Repeat dilation may be needed if dysphagia recurs.
